public_rationale: The filing establishes that free access costs money. It does not quantify hundreds of dollars per user, establish that amount in the target quarter, or classify the industry's revenue as experimental or subsidized. Aggregate losses and retail API-equivalent usage cannot supply the missing calculation. The unspecified cohort, duration and accounting basis prevent a fair monetary verdict.
limitations: The cited filing describes a later state and is context only.
Positive customer ROI would not by itself disprove provider subsidies.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current AI revenues are either chaotically experimental or heavily subsidized, with labs giving away hundreds of dollars per user.

statement.excerpt: Right now, AI revenues are either chaotically experimental or so thoroughly-subsidized that labs are giving away hundreds of dollars a user in the hopes that at some point said user might want to pay even more money for measurably less value, the kind of proposition you make when you think your customers are fucking idiots.

from_speaker: AI revenues are either chaotically experimental or so thoroughly-subsidized
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that revenue depends on unsettled experiments or on substantial service subsidies, rather than established unsubsidized use.
I read hundreds as at least $200, while recognizing that the post supplies neither a user cohort nor a subsidy duration.
Dollars are interpreted as US dollars in the context of OpenAI and Anthropic.
For the ongoing state, I use January–March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication. This does not convert the unspecified subsidy duration into a quarterly threshold.
Subsidy means actual service cost exceeding payment. The retail API value of subscription usage is not itself the provider's cost.
No accounting basis is indicated, preventing a supported or contradicted monetary score under the supplied rules.
criteria.support_condition: Target-period records would need to establish the claimed experimental revenue dependence or actual service costs exceeding payments by hundreds of dollars for an identified user population and duration. Evidence must support the breadth of the either-or assertion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Established production revenue with matching costs and payments showing no qualifying subsidy would counter the categorical either-or assertion. A monetary finding requires a defined cohort, duration and accounting basis.
